problem_context.statement: Given numCourses course IDs from 0 through numCourses - 1 and prerequisite pairs [course, prerequisite], return true if every course can be completed. Each pair means prerequisite must be completed before course.

examples.explanation: Course 0 can be completed before course 1.
The two courses form a directed cycle.

problem_context.title: Course Schedule
constraints: Every course ID in prerequisites is between 0 and numCourses - 1.

expected_approaches.summary: Process all zero-indegree courses and remove their outgoing prerequisite edges.
key_invariants: Only zero-indegree courses are currently eligible.
Processing all nodes proves no directed cycle remains.
expected_approaches.time_complexity: O(V + E), where V = numCourses and E = prerequisites.length
expected_approaches.space_complexity: O(V + E) for adjacency, indegree, and the zero-indegree queue
common_failure_modes: reverse edge direction without changing indegree

expected_approaches.summary: Detect a node encountered on the current DFS path.
key_invariants: UNVISITED nodes have not been explored, ACTIVE nodes are on the current recursion path, and FINISHED nodes are fully explored.
Revisiting ACTIVE proves a directed cycle; reaching FINISHED does not.
expected_approaches.time_complexity: O(V + E), where V = numCourses and E = prerequisites.length
expected_approaches.space_complexity: O(V + E) for adjacency and traversal state, including an O(V) worst-case recursion stack
tradeoffs: Requires distinguishing active state from finished visitation.

reference_solutions.source_code: class Solution { public: bool canFinish(int n,vector<vector<int>> p){vector<vector<int>> g(n);vector<int>d(n);for(auto x:p){g[x[1]].push_back(x[0]);d[x[0]]++;}queue<int>q;for(int i=0;i<n;i++)if(!d[i])q.push(i);int done=0;while(!q.empty()){int u=q.front();q.pop();done++;for(int v:g[u])if(!--d[v])q.push(v);}return done==n;} };

class Solution { public boolean canFinish(int n,int[][] p){java.util.List<Integer>[] g=new java.util.List[n];int[]d=new int[n];for(int i=0;i<n;i++)g[i]=new java.util.ArrayList<>();for(int[]x:p){g[x[1]].add(x[0]);d[x[0]]++;}java.util.ArrayDeque<Integer>q=new java.util.ArrayDeque<>();for(int i=0;i<n;i++)if(d[i]==0)q.add(i);int done=0;while(!q.isEmpty()){int u=q.remove();done++;for(int v:g[u])if(--d[v]==0)q.add(v);}return done==n;} }

invariants.diagnostic_goal: A zero-indegree course has no remaining prerequisite.

complexity_expectations.diagnostic_goal: Each course and prerequisite edge is processed a bounded number of times.

common_misconceptions.diagnostic_goal: Some processable courses do not prove every course can finish.

failure_modes.diagnostic_goal: Build prerequisite to dependent edges consistently.

edge_cases.diagnostic_goal: A course requiring itself is impossible.
With no edges, every course starts at indegree zero.
A cycle in one disconnected component still prevents completing every course.

counterexamples.purpose: A self dependency is a cycle.
The processable component 0 to 1 does not hide the cycle between courses 2 and 3.

constraint_mutations.diagnostic_goal: The same processing can emit one valid ordering.

probe_opportunities.diagnostic_goal: Defend why processing every node is equivalent to no cycle.

sample_phrasings: What does an indegree of zero mean for a course?

expected_good_signals: compares processed count to all courses
sample_phrasings: What must be true about the processed count before you return true?

expected_good_signals: identifies a back edge to active path
weak_or_misconception_signals: treats every visited node as a cycle
sample_phrasings: Why is an active-path revisit different from reaching a finished node?

level_considerations.guidance: Focus on edge direction and complete-processing proof.

pack.reference_reasoning: Kahn processing and DFS active-path detection are both strong valid priors; other correct directed-cycle methods remain valid.

technical_rationale_rubric.technical_issue: Ask which graph structure this visitation state fails to distinguish.

review.description: DFS that marks only visited cannot distinguish an active cycle.
